# 1 Clement Chapter 60 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 60

---

## Council Notes

**On "everlasting constitution" / "everlasting fabric" / "eternal order" (v.1):** EMET: "everlasting constitution." LOGOS: "everlasting fabric." PNEUMA: "eternal order." The Greek *aiōnion systasis* means "eternal establishment/constitution/order." All three are defensible. "Everlasting constitution" (EMET) carries the sense of a divinely established cosmic order and is retained as most precise.

**On the divine attribute catalogue (v.1):** All agents agree on the catalogue of attributes. This passage echoes ancient Jewish berakah (blessing) prayers. The parallel structure should be maintained.

**On "servants and handmaidens" (v.2):** EMET/LOGOS: "servants and handmaidens." PNEUMA: "servants and handmaids." The Greek *doulous kai paidiskas* means male and female servants/slaves. "Servants and handmaids" is the traditional rendering.

**On "rulers and governors" (v.4):** This is the famous early Christian prayer for civil authorities — one of the earliest. It anticipates the prayer for rulers in 1 Tim 2:1–4. All agents preserve "rulers and governors." The Greek *archontas kai hēgoumenous* = rulers and leaders. Both terms are important.

**On format:** SOPHIA follows PNEUMA's poetic layout for this chapter (as agreed in Ch.59 ruling). The Great Prayer continues in poetic form through Ch.61.

---

**60:1** *For you have revealed the everlasting constitution of the world*
*through the things you have fashioned.*
*You, LORD, created the earth.*
*Faithful throughout all generations;*
*righteous in your judgments;*
*wonderful in power and majesty;*
*wise in creating;*
*prudent in establishing all that exists;*
*good in all that is visible;*
*trustworthy among those who trust in you —*
*merciful and compassionate —*
*forgive us our iniquities and unrighteous acts,*
*our transgressions and our failures.*

**60:2** *Reckon not every sin of your servants and handmaids,*
*but cleanse us with the cleansing of your truth.*
*Guide our steps to walk in holiness of heart,*
*to do what is good and well-pleasing*
*before you and before our rulers.*

**60:3** *Yes, O Lord, let your face shine upon us for good in peace.*
*Let your mighty hand protect us.*
*Let your uplifted arm defend us from every sin.*
*Deliver us from those who hate us without cause.*

**60:4** *Give harmony and peace*
*to us and to all who dwell upon the earth,*
*as you gave it to our fathers when they called upon you*
*in faith and in truth —*
*that we may be saved*
*as we render obedience to your all-powerful and most excellent name,*
*and to our rulers and governors upon the earth.*

---

*— SOPHIA*
